newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq accuses U.N. of delaying medical supplies.
newsitem.headline: Iraq accuses U.N. of delaying medical supplies.

text.p: Iraq on Tuesday accused the United Nations sanctions committee of delaying the arrival of medical supplies under an oil-for-food deal signed with the world body.

"Until today (Tuesday) there is only one contract that has been approved by the (U.N.) sanctions committee out of 347 contracts which have arrived there (to the U.N in New York)," Iraqi Health Minister Umeed Madhat Mubarak told Reuters television in Baghdad.

Under the oil agreement between Iraq and the United Nations, which entered into force on Dec. 10, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy humanitarian items to alleviate suffering of Iraqis under U.N. sanctions since Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Under the oil pact, $210 million is allocated for purchasing medical supplies out of $1.3 billion that remains for Iraq after paying 1991 Gulf War reparations.
Iraq last week complained to the United Nations that food supplies were taking too long and urged the world body to speed up their arrival.

Baghdad said it had submitted more than 120 contracts for the purchase of food since the deal went through but only four of them passed by the sanctions committee, overseeing the embargoes on Iraq, due to hurdles placed by the U.S. envoy.
Washington blamed Baghdad for the delay and said Iraq was denying U.N. monitors the full freedom for movement it promised to give under the deal. Baghdad rejected the accusation.
